title: Vector bundle with zero section
statement:
Work in the fixed purity setting [def-pur-conventions]. Let $Z$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, where separatedness refers to the structure morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] and finite type is [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $c\in\mathbb N$.

A vector bundle of constant rank $c$ over $Z$ consists of a scheme morphism $p:E\to Z$, a locally free $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal E$ of constant rank $c$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and an isomorphism over $Z$
$$
\phi:E\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_Z(\mathcal A),\qquad \mathcal A=\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal O_Z}(\mathcal E).
$$
Here $\mathcal A$ and its degree-one map $j:\mathcal E\to\mathcal A$ are the symmetric algebra sheaf constructed in [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction]. Its quasi-coherence and the affine-open identifications $\mathcal A(U)\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_Z(U)}(\mathcal E(U))$ are given by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-affine]. The relative spectrum and its projection $\pi:\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_Z(\mathcal A)\to Z$ are the construction of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec], so $\pi\circ\phi=p$.

The augmentation $\epsilon:\mathcal A\to\mathcal O_Z$ is the unique morphism of $\mathcal O_Z$-algebras with $\epsilon\circ j=0$, using [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-core] with the zero linear map $\mathcal E\to\mathcal O_Z$. Identify $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_Z(\mathcal O_Z)$ with $Z$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2)-(3) on the identity morphism of $Z$, whose direct image algebra is $\mathcal O_Z$. Under that anti-equivalence, the augmentation gives a $Z$-morphism $\bar z:Z\to\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_Z(\mathcal A)$; the zero section of the given bundle is $z=\phi^{-1}\circ\bar z:Z\to E$. The augmentation fixes $\mathcal O_Z$, so $p\circ z=\mathrm{id}_Z$. On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $Z$, the restriction of $z$ is induced by the ring map $\epsilon_U:\operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathcal E(U))\to R$ that fixes constants and sends every degree-one generator to zero. More explicitly, $W_U=p^{-1}(U)$ is affine by the relative-spectrum construction and $\phi$, the opens $W_U$ cover $E$, and $z^{-1}(W_U)=U$ since $p\circ z=\mathrm{id}_Z$. The map $\epsilon_U$ is surjective, since every $r\in R$ is the image of its constant element. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](2), applied to this affine cover of $E$, proves that $z$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

A trivialization of $E$ is an etale morphism $u:Z'\to Z$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] together with an isomorphism of schemes over $Z'$
$$
\tau:E|_{Z'}:=E\times_Z Z'\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf A^c_{Z'},
$$
where restriction means base change [def-pc-base-change] and affine space is [def-sbc-affine-space]. Thus an etale open in this definition means an object $Z'\to Z$ of the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. The chosen isomorphism $\phi$ is part of the vector-bundle data, and determines its zero section.
